screening.reason: Meets inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE-I resting-state fMRI functional connectivity with a hierarchical graph-based deep-learning model (ASD-HNet) for ASD vs healthy-control classification.

evidence_spans.text:
we conducted the experiment on the publicly available ABIDE-I
dataset, including rs-fMRI and phenotypic data of 1112 sub-
jects from 17 different sites (Di Martino et al., 2014; Crad-
dock et al., 2013). In current study, we utilized rs-fMRI data
from 848 subjects, including 396 patients with ASD and 452
health controls (HCs).
evidence_spans.claim: Of the 1112-subject ABIDE-I release across 17 sites, 848 subjects (396 ASD, 452 HC) were used.

assessments.support:
N by diagnosis is given (396 ASD/452 HC of the 1112-subject, 17-site release), but no explicit inclusion/exclusion rule or motion/QC threshold for the 848-subject subset is stated: "we utilized rs-fMRI data
from 848 subjects, including 396 patients with ASD and 452
health controls (HCs)."
DPARSF pipeline steps and the AAL atlas (116 ROIs) are described in detail.
ASD/HC labels are the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis, independent of the connectivity-derived predictors.

Evaluation is a pooled 10-fold cross-validation with no leave-site-out or site-covariate handling described: "we employed the 10-fold cross-
validation strategy to conduct the comparison among dif-
ferent models."

risk_of_bias.summary: Pipeline, atlas and code availability are well documented, but the cohort's exact inclusion/exclusion and QC rule are not given, and the primary evaluation pools all sites in a single 10-fold cross-validation with no site handling.

items.support: N by diagnosis given, no explicit exclusion rule for the 848-subject subset.
Head-movement correction named as a preprocessing step but no motion threshold given.
DPARSF pipeline steps described in detail.
ASD/HC labels are the ABIDE phenotypic diagnosis; this paper does not restate diagnostic criteria.
No leakage-control statement for the 10-fold procedure.
Pooled 10-fold CV with no site handling or leave-site-out.
Code is public; no participant-ID list.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE-I, 848 of the 1112-subject, 17-site release (396 ASD, 452 HC).
narrative_row.methods: DPARSF-preprocessed rs-fMRI; AAL-atlas (116 ROI) functional connectivity; hierarchical functional-gradient-based graph network (ASD-HNet, ROI/community/global scales); pooled 10-fold cross-validation.
narrative_row.outcomes: ASD-HNet achieved accuracy 73.57%, sensitivity 72.63%, specificity 74.90%, F1 71.04%, significantly outperforming eight compared methods (paired t-test p<0.05 each).
narrative_row.key_limitations: No explicit exclusion/QC rule or motion threshold for the 848-subject subset; pooled 10-fold CV with no site handling or stated leakage control.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Code is openly released, aiding reproducibility of the model though not of the exact cohort definition; benchmarked directly against several other ABIDE-I classification methods with matched or overlapping subsets.
